A.explanation: Too small. It does not match the submerged volume of about $0.50 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m}^3$ compared with the total $1.3 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m}^3$.

B.explanation: This is the percentage submerged, since $V_{sub}/V = 0.50/1.3 \approx 0.38$. The question asks for the percentage above the water.

C.explanation: Submerged volume is $5.0 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}^3$, about 38% of the ball, so about 62% is above the water in equilibrium.

D.explanation: Too large. A ball of density about $385 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$ cannot have almost all its $1.3 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m}^3$ volume out of water.

hints: Notice the ball floats in equilibrium, so its weight $mg$ with $m = 0.50 \text{ kg}$ must balance the upthrust from displaced water.
Recall Archimedes principle: upthrust equals weight of displaced water, $\rho_{water} V_{sub} g$ with $\rho_{water} = 1.0 \times 10^3 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$.
First find the submerged volume $V_{sub}$ from the force balance, then compare it with the total $1.3 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m}^3$ and subtract from 100% to get the volume above water.
walkthrough: Identify equilibrium: weight downwards equals upthrust upwards, so $mg = \rho_{water} V_{sub} g$.
Cancel $g$ to get submerged volume: $V_{sub} = m / \rho_{water}$.
Find fraction submerged: $V_{sub}/V = (5.0 \times 10^{-4})/(1.3 \times 10^{-3}) \approx 0.38$, so about 38% is below the surface.
Fraction above water is the remainder: $1 - 0.38 = 0.62$, or about 62%. This is option C.
